messages:
customer_acme: Hey team — started seeing big latency spikes around 2025-09-12T22:10Z. p50 ~30ms -> p99 ~750ms. Our app is sending requests with preferred region header `x-region-prefer: us-west1` but responses show `x-served-region: ap-southeast1` and some retries are getting 401s. Any ideas?

maria-support: Sorry about that. Can you paste a minimal curl example and one trace id from a slow request? Also which API (generate/chat/embeddings)?

customer_acme: Using /v1/generate (completion). Sample curl: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \\n  -H "x-region-prefer: us-west1" \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-rt-1","prompt":"hi"}'``` Trace header from the response: `x-trace-id: rwd-20250912-7b3f2a`. Response headers also had `x-served-region: ap-southeast1` and `x-retry-reason: auth_retry`.

maria-support: Thanks. Devin from SRE, can you take a look?

devin-sre: Looking. I pulled trace rwd-20250912-7b3f2a from our trace store. High-level hop list: `client -> edge-us-west -> route-policy -> egress-gateway-eu -> compute-ap-southeast1`. There's an auth retry at the route-policy stage that triggered fallback selection. Latency added ~260-350ms for the inter-region hop.

kai-platform: That auth_retry flag is interesting. Our current fallback policy for token reauth is set to `fallback: nearest-available` for legacy tenants. If the primary region returns 401 during token validation, the router will try other regions to find a healthy token state. That can unfortunately pick APAC in some weight scenarios.

maria-support: Is that expected behavior? Customer expects `x-region-prefer` to be honored.

kai-platform: Not ideal. `x-region-prefer` is advisory unless tenant has strict routing flag enabled. For ACME account we defaulted to advisory when they were created. We should either: 1) honor region-prefer strictly for this tenant, or 2) narrow fallback to same-continent only.

devin-sre: Repro steps I followed: 1) Sent a request with `x-region-prefer: us-west1` and a short-lived API key that we rotated in us-west. 2) Forced the auth backend to return 401 for the us-west token check. 3) Router attempted reauth and selected eu then ap-southeast for retries based on route weights. Logs: ```[route-policy] trace=rwd-20250912-7b3f2a auth_check=failed region=us-west next_regions=[eu-west1,ap-southeast1] picked=ap-southeast1 latency_ms=320```

amelia-ops: I'm going to apply a tenant-scoped change: set `routing.strict_region_preference=true` for tenant acme and set `fallback.continent_only=true` as a guard. Will canary to 5% first.

maria-support: Thanks Amelia — please post the canary window and results. Customer is eager.

ingest-bot: alert: spike_detected tenant=acme metric=endpoint_p99 duration=15m start=2025-09-12T22:08Z

amelia-ops: Canary applied at 22:35Z to 5% of ACME traffic (route policy version 2025-09-12-ops1). Will monitor p95/p99 for 20 minutes.

devin-sre: After canary I re-ran the forced-401 test: router no longer selects ap-southeast1 for canaried traffic, it fails fast with 401 and returns to client. That removes the cross-region hop. Logged: ```[route-policy] trace=rwd-20250912-8c6d1f auth_check=failed region=us-west next_regions=[] picked=none failfast=true latency_ms=12```

amelia-ops: Escalating change to 100% for ACME at 22:58Z. Patch deployed and rolled to all route-proxies serving tenant.

devin-sre: Monitoring shows p99 dropped from ~750ms -> ~95ms within two minutes after rollout. No more `x-served-region: ap-southeast1` for ACME.

customer_acme: Confirming — latency back to normal, no 401 retries. Thanks team! Any follow-up to prevent recurrence?

kai-platform: Follow-ups: 1) Update tenant onboarding to default `routing.strict_region_preference=true` for customers requesting region pinning. 2) Add a config option `fallback.continent_prefer` not just nearest-available. 3) Add a trace-level alert when route-policy picks a served-region that differs from `x-region-prefer` and adds >100ms extra latency.

maria-support: I'll create a support KB for this pattern (auth rotation causing cross-region fallback) and attach the trace examples.

customer_acme: Appreciated. One ask — could we get an SLA note that region-prefer is respected for our account?

kai-platform: We'll follow up with account team and set tenant-level contract flag.

maria-support: Closing the thread once docs + onboarding ticket created. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
